titre: Agentic design watch for October 19, 2026: a design system must be readable by AI
essentiel: A design system is only "AI-ready" if it has a token layer the agent can refer to.
The Figma agent is out of beta, and Figma specs is presented as a possible source of truth.
Slim day: little usable design content, mostly off-topic LinkedIn profiles.

syntheses.titre: Without a token layer, a design system isn't ready for AI
syntheses.texte: A Substack post published today explains how to check whether a design system is ready for AI. It builds on a five-level model published this summer by Billy Sweetman (Headway). At the lowest level, "Ad hoc", components are copied and rebuilt, with no token to point to. John Rodrigues' masterclass on "AI-ready" design systems goes in the same direction: preparing the system matters as much as the tool.

syntheses.titre: The Figma agent is out of beta and Figma specs aims to become the source of truth
syntheses.texte: According to a masterclass held on October 15, Figma's agent is no longer in beta. Figma also launched Figma specs, presented as the pivot of the source of truth for design systems. On the ecosystem side, Figma announced 20 new MCP partners at Config India (X post of October 15). The question shifts: where should the agent read the system's truth?

tendances.titre: Without a token layer, a design system isn't ready for AI
tendances.texte: A post published today describes a five-level maturity model. At the lowest level, components are copied and rebuilt, with no token to point to. Documentation and tokens become the prerequisite for an AI to iterate cleanly.
